title: UK Backs Robotics Adoption Hubs With £40M in Funding
source_used: The AI Insider (relaying a UK government announcement)
key_facts: The UK government is backing a network of Robotics Adoption Hubs with £40 million to help businesses and public services use robotics and autonomous systems.
Eight hubs are being set up, including projects on surgical robotics, agriculture, manufacturing, waste and recycling, service robots, drones and self-driving vehicles.
Hubs offer expert advice, demonstrations and practical support, and connect users with suppliers, integrators and finance providers.
The government says robotics and autonomous systems could add up to £150 billion to the UK economy by 2035 if adoption is maximised, against an estimated £6.4 billion at current levels.
The programme includes £1.7 million for a national body, led by The Welding Institute with Anglia Ruskin University, and £2.5 million for 12 robotics training projects.
AI Minister Kanishka Narayan said too often businesses do not know where to start.
quote_evidence: The U.K. government is backing a new network of Robotics Adoption Hubs with £40 million to help businesses and public services put robotics and autonomous systems into practical use.

The government said robotics and autonomous systems could add as much as £150 billion to the U.K. economy by 2035 if adoption is maximized, compared with an estimated £6.4 billion at current adoption levels.
why_it_matters_hint: UK firms and public services get advice and demonstrations on adopting robots; the £150 billion figure is a best case.
notes: Government announcement relayed by The AI Insider; the economic figure is the government's projection. The article describes advice and connections, not subsidies for buying robots.
